meta.expect: still today; does not play a later meeting

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm Owen's mother. You asked for this meeting, Hale, so go ahead. I have a client call at 4:40.
Okay. I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me first.
[One week later. Owen has done the rewrite and got 78.]
It's still Tuesday, Hale, and I'm still at this desk. Nobody has agreed to a rewrite, and I haven't had an answer. Who decided on the zero, and why didn't anyone call me first?
So, now that the rewrite is done, are you satisfied?
No rewrite has happened, Hale. The zero is still in the gradebook, and I'm not satisfied with anything yet. Withdraw it, and tell me who decided to enter it without calling me.
[The principal walks in and sits down.]

Nobody has walked in, Hale. It's the two of us, and only what you say out loud counts. I'll be going to the principal's office when we're done, so I'll ask again: who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
